## Outcome

Provide the common admission ledger and scorecard contract used by the six language-family corpus tasks in #262, #263, #264, #265, #266 and #267. Parent: #261. Every registered language is benchmarked using external data and receives its own result row. This issue is backlog specification only; no implementation or benchmark execution is claimed.


Research and backlog specification — 6 November 2026. No implementation or new benchmark execution is authorised by this document.

## Required outcome

Every language ID must have its own external-corpus selection, provenance ledger, applicable oracle, coverage declaration and results row. The 148 handwritten examples already documented are supplementary regression proposals; they do not satisfy external benchmark coverage.

Prioritise recognised, independently maintained evidence in this order, subject to task fit:

1. Established benchmark datasets with usable ground truth: Defects4J, SWE-bench Verified/Multilingual and the RefactoringMiner mapping/refactoring oracles. Use their actual original tasks and source revisions.
2. Standards/conformance suites: Test262, Web Platform Tests, WebAssembly spec tests, YAML Test Suite, CommonMark/GFM, W3C XML tests and related format suites. These establish a different property from repair benchmarks and receive separate scores.
3. Official compiler/runtime/project regression suites: LLVM/Clang, GCC, Roslyn, rustc, Go, Kotlin, Swift, TypeScript and the equivalent authoritative upstream suites for other languages. Preserve original expected diagnostics/outputs and context.
4. Specialist published research datasets, community suites and samples only where needed. Label their status and limitations explicitly; an academic publication, official sample or Hugging Face hosting alone does not establish an industry-standard benchmark.

TPC-H and TPC-DS are respected industry database workloads and useful supplementary SQL complexity/scaling inputs. They do not supply semantic-diff intent labels. Any adapted workload results must be identified as derived experiments and must not imply an official TPC result. Review current toolkit terms and publication rules before reuse.

## Three independent evaluation lanes

| Lane | External input and independent expected result | Report |
|---|---|---|
| Parser/source fidelity | Upstream source fixtures with syntax, diagnostics, tree, typed-value, descriptor or rendering expectations | Applicable feature coverage, acceptance/rejection, lost semantic facts and source-span correctness |
| Change understanding | Original before/after repair, mapping, schema-compatibility or migration fixtures; otherwise reviewed transformations of external source with independently established outcomes | Change-fact precision/recall, entity correspondence, refactoring relations and preservation false alarms |
| Robustness and scaling | External corpus seeds plus bounded grammar-aware mutations, malformed/incomplete input and size/depth/Unicode stress | Crashes, panics, hangs, timeouts, explicit rejection/fallback, coverage, latency and peak memory |

A parser need not execute programs. The reference compiler/interpreter/browser/DB is used outside IntentumDiff to establish the fixture's oracle. Translation to IntentumDiff's semantic tree needs a documented comparison domain; upstream syntax acceptance alone does not prove semantic projection correctness.

Where only generation tasks exist, record that they lack original edit pairs. Where only samples exist, record that no gold oracle has yet been admitted. Never label arbitrary edits meaningful, treat same-output-on-one-input as equivalence, or turn a tool's current output into its own expected answer.

## Admission and data separation

Each case records upstream suite/version, immutable revision, original case/task/commit ID, exact selected source bytes and hashes, original expected output, selected language/dialect, enclosing files/environment, licence and attribution, and the derivation history if modified. Extract the language payload from host-language test wrappers; e.g. C# strings inside Roslyn tests and Q# inside Rust tests must not be benchmarked as the host language.

Separate `upstream_gold`, `reviewed_external_derived`, `external_seed_only`, and `handwritten_regression`. Publish the case count and result for each class. Exclude seed-only and handwritten cases from the external-gold denominator. Maintain task/repository-level holdouts and deduplicate translated or reused tasks across suites.

Each language needs externally sourced evidence of meaningful changes and preservation controls where those claims apply. If its primary corpus provides only single-source conformance cases, require independently reviewed external-derived pairs or an additional repair/refactoring corpus before claiming change-understanding coverage. Missing change labels must be shown as a gap even if the conformance lane passes.

## Per-language scorecard

Required dimensions are `language_id`, parser component identity, core identity, interface, dialect/version, suite, suite revision, case class, change family and evaluation lane. Preserve separate C/C++, JS/TS/TSX, DAX/M, WAT/WAST and Databricks alias routing results even when they share a component. Deduplicate shared source cases when reporting a portfolio total.

Required counts are discovered, eligible, admitted, executed, passed, failed, unsupported, skipped and blocked. Rates must include their denominator. Use null/N/A with a reason for missing evidence, never 0% failures or 100% accuracy for zero cases. No language disappears from the report because its corpus acquisition or environment failed.

Show meaningful-change recall, false alarms on preservation controls, correspondence and explanation-fact precision/recall, span accuracy, invalid-input handling and resource outcomes separately. Preservation does not automatically imply style-only: renames and equivalent rewrites still deserve accurate structural explanations. Report per-language results before any pooled summary, and include macro averages only over an explicitly stated eligible set.

Reference baselines must receive the same source revisions and observation domain. An IntentumDiff score derived from SWE-bench patches is not the SWE-bench repair-agent percentage-resolved. A compiler suite pass is not full language certification. Fuzzer coverage or crash-free duration is not proof of change accuracy.

## Acceptance for future implementation

- [ ] Every one of the 74 registered IDs has an external corpus record and an explicit ready/blocked status.
- [ ] Primary source selection favours recognised benchmarks or authoritative suites over arbitrary mined commits; specialist/candidate exceptions have reasons.
- [ ] At least one admitted external case is actually executed in each claimed supported lane; broad language-hardening claims require a declared construct/change-family coverage target, not a token sample.
- [ ] Each claimed language's change lane includes witnessed meaningful edits and preservation controls, with original upstream and reviewed-derived cases distinguished.
- [ ] Mandatory data/environment failures fail the benchmark job or mark the language blocked; they cannot silently disappear or return empty success.
- [ ] Exact Rust/component outputs are judged against independent source evidence; thin Python/editor parity is measured separately on identical bytes.
- [ ] Small offline CI subsets and expanded runs are versioned; full denominators, exclusions, known failures and holdout policies are published.
- [ ] The public scorecard identifies which suites were adapted and which original benchmark metrics do not apply.

## Known acquisition/oracle gaps

ADF samples, DAXBench, generic prose, PostScript, ReasonML, Squirrel and the inspected Zig seed route need extra acquisition, licensing, fixture or oracle work before they support the intended claims. This is not an exhaustive list of all remaining import work: every selected suite still needs a pinned import and validated adapter. ABAP, Delphi and SAS also have qualified community/runtime profiles rather than a verified general industrial semantic-edit benchmark.

The accompanying all-language table is a selection and admission plan. It contains no fabricated case counts or benchmark scores, and no new results are claimed.
